format: Screenshot receipts, result shown before the process

hook.visual: Phone screen held close, sleep app history showing a wake-up at 3:04am, then 3:11am, then 2:58am, thumb scrolling through them
hook.audio: Three fifty eight. Three eleven. Three oh four. That was my last two weeks.

script: Three fifty eight. Three eleven. Three oh four. That was my last two weeks.
Every night, same thing, awake for an hour, then dead by 11am at my desk.
I didn't buy a supplement for it. I read reviews for about an hour first because I assume all of this is nonsense.
The line that kept coming up on this one was, I stopped waking up at 3am. Same words, over and over.
It's magnesium glycinate. 300mg. No melatonin in it, which is the bit I cared about.
One capsule, half an hour before bed. That's the whole routine.
Nothing happened for the first week, and I nearly binned it.
Then I checked the app again, and that's the part I'll show you.
on_screen_text: 1 hour of reading reviews, not an ad
caption: What time do you wake up in the night? Mine was 3am on the dot.
share_reason: Someone who wakes at the same time every night sends it to their partner or group chat as, this is literally me, look at the times
comment_trigger: Asking what time people wake up gets hundreds of one-word replies, and the deliberate withhold of the final screen makes people ask what happened
why_views: Real timestamps on a real phone read as evidence rather than advertising, and the unresolved final screen keeps people to the last beat.

format: Day-by-day diary where the early days are honestly boring, payoff in the last 20%

hook.visual: Creator in bed, lamp on, holding one capsule up to the camera, slightly annoyed face
hook.audio: Day four of this and I've felt absolutely nothing, so I'm filming the whole thing.

script: Day four of this and I've felt absolutely nothing, so I'm filming the whole thing.
Day five, nothing. Slept badly, woke up at 3am as usual, brilliant.
Day six, I checked the label to see if I'd been taking it wrong. I hadn't. One capsule, 30 minutes before bed.
Day seven, the site does say five to ten days, so fine, I'm not out yet.
Day eight, first night I didn't remember waking up. Could be a fluke.
Day nine, same. Day ten, same.
It's 300mg magnesium glycinate, there's no melatonin in it, so I'm not groggy in the morning, which was my whole worry.
I'm not going to tell you it's magic. I'm telling you it took over a week and I nearly quit on day six.
on_screen_text: day 6: checked I wasn't doing it wrong
day 6 is where most people quit
caption: Anyone else give up on something at day six?
share_reason: Sent by one sceptical friend to another as proof that the honest version of a supplement review exists, and as a warning not to quit early
comment_trigger: The day six quit point is a plainly stated opinion people argue with, plus loads of people reply about the thing they gave up on too soon
why_views: Opening on failure rather than success breaks the pattern of every supplement video and buys enough scepticism credit that people stay for the turn.

format: 3-item ranking of reasons not to buy it, most controversial last

hook.visual: Creator sat on the edge of the bed, product bottle on the duvet beside them, holding up three fingers straight to camera
hook.audio: Three reasons you shouldn't buy the sleep thing I've been taking.

script: Three reasons you shouldn't buy the sleep thing I've been taking.
One. It's slow. Five to ten days before you notice anything. If you want tonight sorted, this isn't it.
Two. It's 24 quid a month on subscription. That's a real cost and I'm not going to pretend it isn't.
Three, and this is the one people don't want to hear.
It will not out-work your phone. If you're scrolling until 1am, which is exactly what you're doing right now, no capsule fixes that.
What it is, is 300mg of magnesium glycinate with no melatonin, so you don't wake up foggy.
The review line that made me try it was, I stopped waking up at 3am. That's the whole promise. That's it.
So if you're still scrolling, reason three is for you.
caption: Reason three is the one nobody likes. What time is it where you are?
share_reason: Sent to the mate who complains about sleep every week but is on TikTok at midnight, as a light callout
comment_trigger: Directly accusing the viewer of scrolling at 1am provokes defensive replies, and the price named out loud starts a worth-it or not argument
why_views: A negative ranking about a product the creator actually uses is a contradiction the brain wants resolved, and calling out the viewer's current behaviour lands mid-scroll.
